content.title: NBA play-in 2026: Suns emphatically end Warriors' season to claim West's final playoff spot, Magic advance in East
content.text: It will be the Phoenix Suns against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the first round of the NBA playoffs, as the Golden State Warriors were only able to muster one wild comeback in the play-in tournament.The Suns took an early lead and held it throughout the rest of the game, emerging with a 111-96 win to take the final playoff spot in the West. They’ll begin their series against the top-seeded Thunder on Sunday, while the Warriors’ season is over.AdvertisementIt was Jalen Green who showed out for the Suns, posting 36 points on 14-of-20 shooting (8-of-14 on 3-pointers) plus 6 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 blocks and 2 steals. That 3-point total tied the play-in tournament record.The Warriors, meanwhile, looked understandably gassed after a furious effort to survive the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday. Stephen Curry posted only 17 points on 4-of-16 shooting with 4 assists and 4 turnovers.Jordan Goodwin came up huge for SunsThe Suns got the win despite down games from both of their leading scorers, Devin Booker and Dillon Brooks. The two men combined for 33 points on 9-of-26 shooting with 12 assists, 6 turnovers and 8 personal fouls.AdvertisementGreen going off helped mitigate that issue, but also big was Jordan Goodwin, who started only 10 games during the regular season but was one of the best players on the floor Friday.The 27-year-old Goodwin posted 19 points on 7-of-11 shooting with 9 rebounds, 6 steals and 2 assists. He was charged with guarding Curry and looked up to the task all night.Jordan. Goodwin.Answering Steph Curry with a triple of his own ... then forces a jump-ball against Curry with his quick hands. The heartbeat of this Suns group. pic.twitter.com/XvGZMmmNcF— Shane Young (@YoungNBA) April 18, 2026What’s next for the Warriors?The loss begins a potentially eventful offseason for Golden State, which is still trying to squeeze some last glory out of Curry’s career and has been previously linked to deals for stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo.Draymond Green, who exited the game via double ejection with Booker at the hands of Scott Foster, only has a player option remaining on his contract and is widely seen as a trade candidate, while head coach Steve Kerr’s contract is expiring.AdvertisementAfter the game, both men acknowledged that an exit from the franchise is possible after a decade of working together.Magic blow out Hornets in the EastEarlier in the night, the Orlando Magic had little trouble with the Charlotte Hornets to win the final playoff spot in the East. They were up by 22 at the end of the first quarter, up 31 at halftime and dominated in pretty much every phase of the game.The Magic will now face the Detroit Pistons in the first round, while the Hornets’ season is over.
